subject: AcmeCloud private offer: rev-share uplift & payment-term alignment request
messages:
From: Ryan Kelly <ryan.kelly@acmecloud.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement AcmeCloud <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: rev-share uplift + payment-term alignment

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. AcmeCloud is ready to move forward with Redwood on a private offer listing in AWS Marketplace, but procurement has two non-standard asks we need you to evaluate:

- Rev-share: They are requesting a 60% rev-share to AcmeCloud (first 12 months) due to bundling with our managed services.
- Payment terms: Procurement prefers Net60 for the first year (company policy).

We understand these are out-of-band. We can be flexible on upfront commitment and are open to a $250k upfront credit that gets reconciled against usage.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can approve those two points or if you need executive sign-off? We need to finalize the private offer with AWS by 11/10 to hit their internal procurement window. Draft attached.

Attachments: AcmeCloud_PrivateOffer_Draft_v3.pdf, AWS_PO_Revshare_Schedule.xlsx

Thanks,
Ryan Kelly
Sr Dir, Strategic Partnerships
AcmeCloud
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private offer: rev-share uplift + payment-term alignment

Team — forwarding AcmeCloud's ask. High-level thoughts below; please review and flag any legal/finance blockers.

Summary of external ask:
- 60% rev-share to AcmeCloud for first 12 months
- Net60 payment terms
- $250k upfront credit proposed (reconcilable)

Impact and recommendation:
- Revenue/cost: 60% rev-share materially reduces Redwood gross on this listing. At our projected ARR it would drop unit contribution below our min threshold.
- Marketplace constraints: AWS will only approve private offers that meet their payout and listing rules; large rev-share percentages are uncommon but possible with approval.

My proposed concession (requesting exec clearance):
1) Cap rev-share to 50% for months 1–6, then 35% months 7–12 (sliding model).
2) Limit upfront credits to $200k and structure as a usage credit (not refundable).
3) Hold payment terms at Net45 (standard), allow Net60 only if Finance signs off on AR risk and we receive a 12-month minimum commit (minimum spend commitment attached).

Next steps for approvals:
- I need explicit executive approval for any rev-share >45% OR payment-term >45 days.
- Olga: please model exposure and add standard legal guardrails (indemnities, audit rights; remove resale carveouts that increase leakage).
- Monica/karthik: confirm commission routing and partner-credit treatment.

Goal: get final position to AcmeCloud by EOD 11/04 so they can submit to AWS marketplace by 11/10.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private offer: rev-share uplift + payment-term alignment

Markus / team — ran the numbers and left some notes in the attached model. Key points:

- If we agree to 60% rev-share for 12 months, expected contribution margin for the listing drops ~42% vs baseline (assumes $3.2M GTY first 12 months).
- Sliding model proposed by Markus (50% -> 35%) improves margin by ~12 percentage points vs flat 60% request.
- Upfront credit: $250k vs $200k shifts cashflow by ~$50k; finance prefers smaller credit and escrow-style offset.
- Payment terms: Net60 pushes cash conversion days up ~30 days; we estimate ~$600k incremental working capital need for year 1. Finance sign-off required.

Suggested alternative for faster approval:
- Offer 55% rev-share for months 1–3, 40% months 4–12; cap credits at $200k; require minimum 9-month commit and Net45.
- If AcmeCloud insists on Net60, require a fee equivalent (1.5% monthly) to offset AR risk.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ACME-2026-1123), draft DocuSign in Drive.

I'll prepare a one-page executive memo with exposure numbers if that helps.

Monica Patel
Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: AWS_PO_Revshare_Schedule.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private offer: rev-share uplift + payment-term alignment

Markus / all — reviewed the ask and ops/finance analysis. Executive decision below so we can get this moving.

Executive clearance (approved with conditions):
- Rev-share: approve a temporary concession of 55% for months 1–3, stepping to 40% for months 4–12. No flat 60% for 12 months.
- Upfront credit: cap at $200k and structure as usage credit only. Any unused credit forfeits after 12 months.
- Payment terms: keep Net45. If customer insists on Net60, we will accept Net60 only if AcmeCloud signs an AR fee of 1.5%/month on outstanding balance and provides a purchase-order-backed commit for at least 9 months.
- Legal: Olga to add audit rights, quarterly usage reconciliation, and a strict resale carveout (no bundling that bypasses marketplace reporting).
- Marketplace: confirm with AWS ops that this rev-share schedule is acceptable for private offers; if AWS pushes back, revert to 50%/35% sliding model.

Action items:
- Markus: send the updated private offer terms to AcmeCloud by noon PT 11/05 and copy Marketplace ops.
- Olga: prepare final redlines and update DocuSign template; target 11/09 signature.
- Monica: finalize revenue impact memo for Finance; include AR exposure and commission routing.

This is a one-time executive concession to secure the strategic placement with AcmeCloud. If any material deviations are requested by the customer or AWS, escalate to me immediately.

Lauren Bishop
VP Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
